newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Ahold net jumps on U.S. acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Ahold net jumps on U.S. acquisition.

text.p: Dutch retail company Koninklijke Ahold NV announced sharply higher third-quarter profits Wednesday, largely due to extra sales following the acquisition of the Stop & Shop chain in the United States.
It said 1996 full-year net earnings would be significantly higher than last year.
Ahold, which bought Stop & Shop for $2.9 billion earlier this year, said net profit jumped to 156.4 million guilders ($91.41 million) from 101.6 million guilders ($59.4 million).
Net earnings per share rose to 0.93 guilders (54 cents) from 0.81 guilders (47 cents) in the 1995 period.
Third-quarter revenue increased to 9.27 billion guilders ($5.4 billion) from 6.94 billion guilders ($4.06 billion), largely due to the extra sales generated by Stop & Shop.

Ahold, which owns the biggest Dutch supermarket company, Albert Heijn, previously said the Stop & Shop acquisition, included in Ahold's figures for the first time in the third quarter, would further boost profits.
"Further growth of earnings per share is expected to be positively influenced by the acquisition of Stop & Shop," Ahold said in a statement.
The profits were in line with analysts' forecasts.
